pr_body:
1. Have all markdown rendering go through a single `markdown.Render()` function, rather than through a bunch of `RenderWith...` functions.
2. Simplify detecting the terminal theme when rendering Markdown.
3. Preserve hard line breaks from GitHub-flavored Markdown. Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1110

Ref. https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/releases/tag/v0.4.0

issue_context.title: Markdown rendering show softbreaks
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
On the web interface, lines that don't end with at least 2 spaces are not joined.

```shell
$ gh --version
gh version 0.9.0 (2020-05-26)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

If you run the following
command it your shell,
theses lines will be joined.

```shell
$ gh issue -R cli/cli view 1110
```
comments:
Good catch, thank you!

GitHub UI has some extensions on top of the "vanilla" Markdown behavior: it preserves hard line breaks, for one. The Markdown library that we are using in CLI does not preserve hard line breaks, but maybe we could instruct it do to so? PRs welcome!
@mislav  I would still like to give it a shot on this issue :).
@sibis are you working on this? Because I figured out a way as well to solve this problem.

So i had a look into this and glamour doesn't have the option to preserve newlines. I found [this line][glamour-flag] in their code which explicitly turns newline preserving off.

Just to test i did a build with a local version of glamour with that flag set to true and it did work as expected.

Could probably ask them if that can be exposed as a configurable option

[glamour-flag]: https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/blob/9c39c0ec765167910062dce222626b9de9a8c826/ansi/paragraph.go#L41

Update: the ability to preserve new lines was added with charmbracelet/glamour#115. Once a release is published we will be able to update our dependency and utilize `WithPreservedNewLines()` with our renderer.

cc @mislav

review_comments: Looks like `io.DetectTerminalTheme()` got dropped here, is it no longer necessary?

Good catch! It's not necessary to explicitly call DetectTerminalTheme when no output pager is used, but I have assumed that `TerminalTheme()` does automatic detection already. It didn't, so I've pushed a commit to make `TerminalTheme` invoke `DetectTerminalTheme` if that hasn't happened yet 👍
